title: Color / UI palette — RGB specifications

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: RGB

slide_intent: Separate interface color roles from the full expressive palette, because users need action and status signals to stand out from structural surfaces.
strategic_value: A restrained blue, gray and alert set can make IBM products feel related while leaving functional signals distinct.
demonstration: The RGB UI table presents blue and neutral-gray ramps with black and white, plus four alert swatches at the right.
practical_value: Choose the RGB value within the UI subset after deciding whether the element is structural, actionable or a status signal.

content_islands.name: Encoding tabs
content_islands.spec: Show RGB selected above the table.

content_islands.name: Blue and neutral ramps
content_islands.spec: Align the long blue and gray columns from black through numbered grades to white.

content_islands.name: Alert subset
content_islands.spec: Place red Alert 60, green Alert 50, orange Alert 40 and yellow Alert 30 in the shorter right column.

ingredient.name: UI palette roles
ingredient.application: Use neutral gray to organize zones and core blue for primary action; use additional colors sparingly and purposefully.
ingredient.scope: The roles come from the accompanying Color in UI guidance; the RGB table supplies values and does not prescribe area percentages.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying Color in UI text assigns neutral grays to organization and core blue to primary action so the identity carries into interaction.
reference_purposes.Expression: The two ramps and four alerts demonstrate the narrower IBM UI color vocabulary.
reference_purposes.Application: The RGB tab provides digital channel values for the UI subset.
